docs.text: DomainMOD gives you a few options for adding your domains, so you should read through the below sections to determine which will work best for you. Note Before adding your domains to DomainMOD you must first create some Assets. If you've just finished installing you should visit the First Run section, which will walk you through creating the Assets that are required to start using DomainMOD. Alternatively, you can use the CSV Importer to import all of your domain data without having to create any Assets first. CSV Importer The CSV Importer allows you to import all of your domain data into DomainMOD using a CSV template. This is a brand new feature as of DomainMOD v4.19, but all testing has gone very well, and I've personally imported quite a few test CSV files with 100% accuracy. Keep in mind that the CSV Importer only imports new domains, it does not update domains that are already in your DomainMOD database. Add domains using the CSV Importer » Domain Queue One of the easiest options for adding domains is to use the Domain Queue, which allows you to supply a list of domains and let DomainMOD take care of the rest (and in some cases you don't even need to supply the list of domains, it will be automatically retrieved from your registrar account). If your registrar has an API that DomainMOD supports, the Domain Queue uses it to retrieve the information required to add your domains, so before using this option make sure your API credentials have been saved with your registrar account. If your registrar isn't supported, you can still paste in a list of your domains, and DomainMOD will look up their details using RDAP, the public replacement for WHOIS, or WHOIS itself for domains that RDAP doesn't cover. Add domains using the Domain Queue » Bulk Updater The Bulk Updater also allows you to supply a list of domains to be added, however you need to manually choose the options for the domains you're adding, and all of the domains will have the same settings. The Bulk Updater generally works best if you're adding a list of newly registered domains, since they will have the same expiry date and will generally have the same settings. Add domains using the Bulk Updater » Manually Domains can also be added one-by-one, which allows you to choose custom settings for each domain. Adding A Domain Manually Click on Domains on the main menu. Click the Add Domain button on the Domains page. Enter the Domain that you want to add. Fill in all of the relevant details for the domain, such as the expiry date, registrar account, DNS profile, and so on. Click the Add Domain button. That's it, your domain has been added to DomainMOD! Note If this is the first time you've added a domain from this registrar with this TLD you will need to enter the fees associated with this registrar/TLD combination. After adding the domain you will be presented with a notice that will walk you through how to add the new fee. Until the fee is added, the domain is hidden from the Domains list, and you can find the fees still to add in the Missing Fees section of Assets -> Domain Fees ( Assets -> SSL Fees for SSL certificates). UPDATE: As of v4.23.0, if you don't care about keeping track of fees, you can now set all missing fees to 0 with the click of a button.

docs.text: Custom Fields Custom Fields help extend the functionality of DomainMOD by allowing the user to create their own data fields. For example, if you wanted to keep track of which domains are currently setup in your Analytics software, you could create a new Analytics check box field and start tracking this information for each of your domains. Combine Custom Fields with the ability to update them with the Bulk Updater *, and the sky's the limit in regards to what data you can easily track! As of v4.27.0, there are custom fields for hosting services too, in Administration -> Custom Hosting Fields , alongside Custom Domain Fields and Custom SSL Fields . When you export your domain, hosting, or SSL certificate data, the information contained in your custom fields will automatically be included in the exported data. As of v4.27.0, you can also filter the Domains and SSL Certificates lists by custom field, in the Custom Fields section of the filter panel. A check box field has a Value menu ( Yes or No ). Text fields, text areas, and URLs have a Contains box, and dates and time stamps have a Between range. Every type except check boxes also has a Filled In menu ( Filled in or Empty ). Custom Field Types: Check Box, Date, Text Field, Text Area, Time Stamp, URL Note As of v4.13, DomainMOD has the ability to display your Custom Field data on the main Domain and SSL Certificate pages, and as of v4.27.0 on the main Hosting page. Note * The Bulk Updater currently only allows you to update Custom Domain Fields, but not Custom Hosting Fields or Custom SSL Certificate Fields. Task Scheduler The Task Scheduler ( Administration -> Task Scheduler ) runs DomainMOD's system jobs, such as processing the Domain Queue, sending expiration emails, and building the Data Warehouse. In order for it to work, you must set up the cron job that comes with DomainMOD, and you can also limit who can run it with a Task Scheduler Key . If you installed DomainMOD using Docker, you don't need to set up the cron job, since the container already runs the Task Scheduler every 10 minutes. Each task can be disabled or enabled, and Run Now runs it straight away. As of v4.27.0, Disable All at the top of the page disables every task that isn't running at the time, and once they're all disabled, Enable All turns them back on. These are the tasks, in the order the Task Scheduler page lists them: Domain Queue Processing (every 5 minutes): looks up the domains in the Domain Queue and adds them to DomainMOD. SSL Queue Processing (every 5 minutes): reads the certificates of the sites in the SSL Queue and adds them to DomainMOD. Send Expiration Email (daily): emails everyone who's subscribed about upcoming domain, hosting service, and SSL certificate renewals. Users can subscribe in their User Profile, and administrators can set the From address and the number of days the email covers in System Settings. Update Conversion Rates (daily): gets the current currency conversion rates and updates every user's costs. Users can set their currency in their User Profile. System Cleanup (daily): converts domains to lowercase, checks that every TLD is correct, and records the status of each domain in your segments, which keeps segment filtering up to date. It also checks the domain, SSL certificate, and fee data against each other, deletes unused domain and SSL fees, updates the hosting services' costs from their fees, and removes change history older than the time set in System Settings. Check For New Version (daily): checks whether a newer version of DomainMOD is available to download. Data Warehouse Build (daily): rebuilds the Data Warehouse , so it has the latest information from your servers. Refresh Domains (every 10 minutes, off by default): as of v4.27.0, checks the expiry date and DNS servers of each live domain (every domain that isn't Expired or Sold), a few domains at a time, and records any changes in the Change History as Scheduled Refresh. When DomainMOD supports the registrar's API and the domain's registrar account has its API details filled in, the registrar's API is used, and it can also update WHOIS privacy and auto-renewal. Otherwise, or if the API can't be used, public RDAP data is used, or WHOIS for TLDs without RDAP, and an RDAP server can pass the lookup on to another server, such as the registrar's. The transfer lock is checked using RDAP. When there's time, the domain's live DNS (its name servers, IP addresses, and mail servers) is also looked up through your server's own DNS resolver, whose operator can see the names being checked. Domains are checked about once a week, and daily in the last 60 days before they expire. A failed check is tried again after a day, then less often each time, up to 30 days, and a domain whose RDAP or WHOIS server is busy waits an hour. See Refreshing Domains . Check Watch List (every 10 minutes): as of v4.27.0, checks the domains on the Watch List with public RDAP and WHOIS servers, a few at a time: weekly while a registered domain is far from expiry, daily in its last 60 days before expiry and in most other stages, and every few hours once it's close to dropping. As of v4.26.0, Last run of cron.php on the Task Scheduler page shows when cron.php last ran, or Never . When you upgrade to v4.26.0, Last run of cron.php is set to the time of the upgrade if the Task Scheduler had run before, so a working cron job isn't reported as stopped before its next run. If any tasks are enabled and cron.php last ran more than two hours ago, administrators see a warning on the Dashboard and the Task Scheduler page, with a link to the cron job instructions. Until it runs again, expiration emails and the Import Queue only run when you use Run Now . If tasks are enabled and cron.php has never run, the Task Scheduler page shows a note explaining how to set it up, and administrators see it on the Dashboard too whenever the Getting Started checklist isn't shown. If every task is disabled, neither page warns you. As of v4.25.0, each daily task runs at the same local time all year, including across daylight saving time changes. When you set a daily task's run time, it's saved in your own time zone (from your user settings), and the Task Scheduler page shows each daily task's run time along with its time zone. Changing your time zone later doesn't move tasks that are already set, so set their run times again if you want them to follow your new time zone. When you upgrade to v4.25.0, existing daily tasks keep running at the same moment, using the time zone of the user who installed DomainMOD (or of the first administrator). Tools As of v4.23.0, to check that DomainMOD can send email, open Administration -> Tools and click Send Test Email . A test email is sent to your own email address.

docs.text: As of v4.14, DomainMOD has a Backup & Restore utility. This feature enables you to perform complete backups and restores of your DomainMOD database. This allows you to export your entire system in a single file so that it can easily be backed up and/or restored, which is helpful if you want to perform regular backups of your data, you need to move DomainMOD to a new server, or you want to change your installation method. This process backs up the data saved in your database. If you also want to save your database connection information, you should back up your /_includes/config.inc.php file. Note Backups are created in PHP's temporary folder, which must be outside your web root, and are deleted as soon as they've been sent to your browser. Restores are refused if PHP's upload folder (upload_tmp_dir) is inside your web root. If you're unsure how to check this, your web hosting provider should be able to assist you. Backup To back up your DomainMOD database: Login to DomainMOD as an administrator Navigate to Administration -> Backup & Restore In the Backup section, click the Backup Entire Database button At this point you will be prompted to download the file domainmod-backup.sql, which contains a copy of your entire database Restore Warning Before restoring your DomainMOD database, ensure that you're restoring a database that is of the same version as the software that you're restoring it to. For example, if you were using DomainMOD v4.14 when you backed up your database, you must restore that database to an installation of DomainMOD v4.14. To restore your DomainMOD database: Login to DomainMOD as an administrator Navigate to Administration -> Backup & Restore In the Restore section, click the Choose File button and then select the domainmod-backup.sql file that you want to restore Click the Restore Entire Database button Once the restore is complete, you will automatically be logged out of DomainMOD. You should now be able to log in using the accounts that you just restored. As of v4.27.0, restores need DomainMOD's temp folder to be writable by the web server. When you restore a backup, the Change History becomes the backup's own. If a Restore Doesn't Finish If a restore stops part-way (for example, if the server times out), DomainMOD stays closed until it's finished. An administrator can open Administration -> Backup & Restore and click Finish Restore , or run php restore.php --recover in DomainMOD's folder on the server, as the web server's user (use this if you can't sign in). The cron job can also finish it when it runs cron.php from the command line or with a Task Scheduler Key , and then logs any warning in the server's error log. Finishing a restore doesn't redo the import, so if DomainMOD or the error log says the database may be partly restored, restore a complete backup before going on. Restoring a Large Backup If a backup is too large to upload, you can restore it on the server instead. Keep the backup file in a private folder outside your web root. Stop the cron job, then run this in DomainMOD's folder as the web server's user. --temp-dir is a private folder outside your web root that the web server's user can write to, where a copy of the backup is kept during the restore. Start the cron job again once the restore has finished. php restore.php /path/to/private/folder/domainmod-backup.sql --temp-dir=/path/to/private/folder Migrating Warning Before migrating it's strongly recommended that you backup your DomainMOD installation directory and database. If something goes wrong during the migration process there may be no way to recover your data, and having a backup of your installation directory and database will allow you to easily restore your data. The Backup & Restore instructions can be found here . To migrate your DomainMOD installation from one server to another: [Old Server] Upgrade to the newest version of DomainMOD [Old Server] Export a copy of your DomainMOD database using the above Backup feature [New Server] Download and install the newest version of DomainMOD [New Server] Login to DomainMOD and navigate to Administration -> Backup & Restore [New Server] In the Restore section, click the Choose File button and then select the domainmod-backup.sql file that you want to restore [New Server] Click the Restore Entire Database button [New Server] Once the restore is complete you will automatically be logged out of DomainMOD. You should now be able to login using the accounts that you just restored. That's it! DomainMOD has now been migrated to your new server.

docs.text: The Bulk Updater allows you add or modify multiple domains at the same time, whether it's a couple dozen or a couple thousand, all with a few clicks. Using the Bulk Updater is simple, it's just like adding or modifying a single domain, but instead of supplying one domain you supply a list of domains, and the Bulk Updater does the rest. Usage For this example we're going to use the Bulk Updater to add domains. However, it can also be used to renew domains, change the status of the domains, change the category, DNS profile, and hosting service of the domains, and so on. Adding Domains Using The Bulk Updater Click on Bulk Updater on the main menu. On the dropdown menu on the Bulk Updater page, choose Add Domains . In the Domains to add text area, paste in a list of domains that you want to add, one domain per line. Fill in all of the relevant details for the domain, such as the expiry date, registrar account, DNS profile, and so on. Click the Add Domains button. That's all there is to it, you've just added some domains in bulk! Finding Domains As of v4.27.0, every action except Add Domains has a Find a domain to add to the list box above the list of domains. For Update Custom Domain Field , the box is on the second step, with the list. Type part of a domain name, then pick it from the results, which show each domain's status, to add it to the list as a new line. You can still type or paste domains straight into the list. Changing the Hosting Service As of v4.27.0, the Change Hosting Service action links every domain on the list to the hosting service you choose. Choose None to remove their links. Cancelled services aren't offered. Add Domains also has an optional Hosting Service menu.

docs.text: As of v4.27.0, DomainMOD keeps a change log (or audit trail) of the changes made to your domains, hosting services , SSL certificates, and watched domains : what changed, the old and new values, when the change happened, who made it, and what made it. Changes are recorded from the add and edit pages, Refresh and the scheduled Refresh Domains task, the Bulk Updater, the CSV Importer, the Domain Queue and SSL Queue, Mark Renewed on a hosting service, asset and fee changes, deleted custom fields, maintenance, and database upgrades. The history starts when DomainMOD is installed, or when an administrator runs Upgrade Database for v4.27.0, so changes made before then aren't listed. Viewing Changes Click Change History on the main menu. Every user can see it, including read-only users. The newest changes come first, with these columns: When , Item , Type , What Changed , From , To , Source , By , and Note . Changes that DomainMOD made itself, such as a scheduled refresh, show DomainMOD in the By column. When one action changed several things, such as a Bulk Updater action, its Source shows a link such as "25 changes to 25 items", which lists every change it made. The Reporting page's Recent Domain Changes tile opens the list with the last 30 days of domain changes. Filters The list shows the last 30 days to start with. You can narrow it down with these filters, then click Apply filters : Type : Domain, Hosting Service, SSL Certificate, or Watched Domain Item Name : part of a domain, hosting service, or certificate name Source : where the change came from, such as Add or Edit Page, Bulk Updater, Refresh, or Scheduled Refresh By : a user, or DomainMOD What Changed : a field, such as Expiry Date or DNS Profile, or one of your custom fields Date : Today, Last 7 Days, Last 30 Days, Last 90 Days, All Time, or a Custom Range Each filter in use is shown above the list, where you can remove it, and Clear filters removes them all. Exporting Click Export to download the changes the list is showing, with your filters applied, as a CSV file. The export also includes each item's ID, the stored values, and, for an added or deleted item, a snapshot of its values, so a deleted item's details can be recovered (a very large item's snapshot may be shortened or leave some fields out). On the Edit Pages The domain, hosting service, SSL certificate, and watched domain edit pages each have a Change History section with that item's recent changes, and a link to see all of them on the Change History page. On a live domain's page (one that isn't Expired or Sold), the section also shows the domain's automatic check status, such as when it was last checked and when its next check is due. How Long Changes Are Kept Administrators can set how long changes are kept in Administration -> System Settings , under Change History : 1, 2, 3, 5, or 10 years, or forever. The default is 3 years. Older changes are removed by the daily System Cleanup task. The change history is included in backups, so a shorter time keeps them smaller, and Administration -> Backup & Restore shows how much of the database it takes up. Restores When you restore a backup , the Change History becomes the backup's own, and the Change History page shows a note such as "This database was restored from a backup on 2027-01-15", since changes made between the backup and the restore aren't shown. The changes recorded before the restore are removed if the backup has no change history (such as one from before v4.27.0), was incomplete, or came from a newer version of DomainMOD. They're also removed if the restore didn't finish or its result couldn't be verified. The page says why, and the Refresh Domains task is turned off, so an administrator should enable it again in the Task Scheduler if it was in use, once a complete backup has been restored if the database may be partly restored.

docs.text: Pull Requests Before submitting a pull request , please contact the maintainers of the repository to discuss the change. As much as we appreciate you wanting to contribute, we don't want you to waste your time working on a change or new feature that won't get implemented (such as a feature that's already in progress). Feature requests live only in the Support Portal, so other users can vote on them. If we need to look at your database to help, we'll arrange a safe, temporary way to do it privately. If you're a developer and can point to the code, you can submit a GitHub issue instead. Please report each bug in one place only, not both. Remove any domains, usernames, API keys, and other private details first. Before submitting, please search the existing issues to make sure it hasn't already been reported. Security Issues Please don't report security vulnerabilities in a public issue or in the Support Portal. See our security policy for how to report them privately.

docs.text: This section of the User Guide details how to add various Assets to DomainMOD, such as your Account Owners, Domain Registrars, Domain Registrar Accounts, Hosting Providers, and so on. If you've just finished installing DomainMOD please see the First Run section for instructions on how to get up-and-running. Add An Owner Click on Assets on the main menu. Under Shared , click Account Owners . Click the Add Owner button. Enter the Owner's Name. Click the Add Owner button. Add a Domain Registrar Click on Assets on the main menu. Under Domains , click Domain Registrars . Click the Add Registrar button. Enter the Registrar's Name and then click the Add Domain Registrar button. And that's all there is to it, you've just added your first Domain Registrar! Now it's time to add your first Domain Registrar Account. Add a Domain Registrar Account Click on Assets on the main menu. Under Domains , click Domain Registrar Accounts . Click the Add Registrar Account button. Choose the Domain Registrar and Account Owner that this registrar account belongs to, enter your account Username, and then click the Add Registrar Account button. Add a Hosting Provider Click on Assets on the main menu. Under Hosting , click Hosting Providers . Click the Add Hosting Provider button. Enter the Hosting Provider's Name and then click the Add Hosting Provider button. Now it's time to add your first Hosting Account. Add a Hosting Account Click on Assets on the main menu. Under Hosting , click Hosting Accounts . Click the Add Account button. Choose the Hosting Provider and Account Owner that this hosting account belongs to, enter your account Username, and then click the Add Hosting Account button. Add a Hosting Service Type DomainMOD comes with a set of service types, such as Shared, VPS, and Email, so you only need to add one if none of them fit. Click on Assets on the main menu. Once you have a hosting account, you can start adding your hosting services . Add an SSL Provider Click on Assets on the main menu. Under SSL Certificates , click SSL Providers . Click the Add SSL Provider button. Enter the SSL Provider's Name and then click the Add SSL Provider button. Now it's time to add your first SSL Provider Account. docs.text: The CSV Importer allows you to import all of your domain data into DomainMOD using a CSV template. This is a brand new feature as of DomainMOD v4.19, but all testing has gone very well, and I've personally imported quite a few test CSV files with 100% accuracy. Keep in mind that the CSV Importer only imports new domains, it does not update domains that are already in your DomainMOD database. You can import as little or as much domain information as you want. Technically you can fill in nothing but a list of domains, and it will import just fine, but DomainMOD will need to create a bunch of generic Assets for you. It's ok though, even if you go this route it's pretty easy to update the information that DomainMOD creates for you. Regardless of how well testing has gone so far, we always recommended that you perform a full backup of your existing DomainMOD database before attempting a CSV Import, just in case something goes wrong and you need to recover. Note CSV imports are refused if PHP's upload folder (upload_tmp_dir) is inside your web root. If you're unsure how to check this, your web hosting provider should be able to assist you. Usage Once logged into DomainMOD, click Domains in the main menu and then click CSV Importer in the menu beside the Add Domain button. If you haven't added any domains yet, click Import from a CSV file instead on the Domains page (shown before you've added a registrar), or CSV Importer in the Dashboard's Getting Started checklist (if you've hidden the checklist, you can turn it back on in Settings -> Display Settings ). You will then be walked through how to import your domain data using our CSV Import Template. CSV Import Template Click here to download the sample CSV Import Template file. Warning The columns in the CSV Import Template must remain as-is. If there are an incorrect number of columns, or the columns are not in the correct order, the CSV import will fail. Template Columns Below is a list of all the columns that appear in the CSV Import Template file, along with a description of what the column is for. The only required column is the domain column, but the more information you enter into the CSV file, the more complete your DomainMOD installation will be. Domain Fields domain ( required ) The domain name. expiry_date The domain's expiry date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD function The function/purpose of the domain. auto_renewal Is auto renew enabled? Options (Numeric): 0, 1 Options (Text): NO, YES (text options are case-insensitive) privacy Is WHOIS privacy enabled? Options (Numeric): 0, 1 Options (Text): NO, YES (text options are case-insensitive) status The domain's status. Options (Numeric): 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10 Options (Text): EXPIRED, ACTIVE, PENDING (TRANSFER), PENDING TRANSFER, PENDING (RENEWAL), PENDING RENEWAL, PENDING (OTHER), PENDING OTHER, PENDING (REGISTRATION), PENDING REGISTRATION, SOLD (text options are case-insensitive) registration_fee The cost of the domain's initial registration. renewal_fee The cost of the yearly domain renewal. transfer_fee The cost that the domain's current registrar charges to transfer this TLD in. privacy_fee The cost of WHOIS privacy for the domain. miscellaneous_fee Any additional fees related to the domain. fee_currency The currency for the domain's fees. Example: USD domain_ip_address_name The name you want to assign to the domain's IP address. domain_ip_address The domain's IP address. domain_ip_address_rdns The reverse DNS of the domain's IP address. domain_ip_address_notes Any notes you have for the domain's IP address. domain_notes Any notes you have for the domain. Domain Category Fields category The name of the category that the domain belongs to. category_stakeholder The individual or company responsible for the specific domain category. category_notes Any notes you have for the domain's category. Web Hosting Provider Fields hosting_provider , hosting_provider_url , hosting_provider_notes As of v4.27.0, these columns are ignored, but they're kept so that older files still import. After importing, you can link your domains to a hosting service with the Bulk Updater . Domain Registrar Fields registrar_name The domain registrar's name. registrar_url The domain registrar's URL. registrar_notes Any notes you have for this domain's domain registrar. Domain Registrar Account Fields registrar_account_owner The individual or company that technically owns the domain registrar account. registrar_account_owner_notes Any notes you have about the domain registrar account owner. registrar_account_email_address The email address for the domain registrar account. registrar_account_username The username for the domain registrar account. registrar_account_password The password for the domain registrar account. registrar_account_account_id The account ID for the domain registrar account. registrar_account_reseller The reseller status for the domain registrar account. Options (Numeric): 0, 1 Options (Text): NO, YES (text options are case-insensitive) registrar_account_reseller_id The reseller ID for the domain registrar account. registrar_account_notes Any notes you have for the domain registrar account. api_app_name Certain domain registrars require you to supply an API app name in order to use their API. api_key Most domain registrars require you to supply an API key in order to use their API. api_secret Most domain registrars require you to supply an API secret in order to use their API. api_ip_address_name Some registrars require you to restrict your API access to specific IP addresses. This is the name you want to assign to that IP address. api_ip_address The API IP address. api_ip_address_rdns The reverse DNS of the API IP address. api_ip_address_notes Any notes you have for the API IP address. DNS Fields dns_profile_name The name you want to assign to the grouping of DNS servers used by this domain. dns_server_1 - dns_server_10 The (2-10) DNS servers used by this domain. dns_ip_1 - dns_ip_10 The (2-10) IP addresses used by this domain's DNS servers. dns_notes Any notes you have for the set of DNS servers.

The Dashboard Page Totals : how many domains, hosting services, SSL certificates, and sold domains you have. Pending : how many domains, hosting services, and SSL certificates have each Pending status. Renewal Costs, Next 12 Months : a chart of what your renewals will cost each month. The Getting Started Checklist On a new installation, the Dashboard shows a Getting Started checklist, which walks you through adding your registrar, your registrar account, your fees, and your domains. Administrators also get a step for setting up the cron job . Each step ticks itself off as you go, and the checklist goes away once you've added your first domain, hosting service, or SSL certificate. If you'd rather not see it, click Hide this checklist . docs.text: DomainMOD has a Data Warehouse framework built right into it, which allows you to import the data stored on your web server. Currently the only web servers that are supported are ones that run WHM/cPanel. If your web server doesn't run WHM/cPanel, or you don't want to import your web server data into DomainMOD, you can ignore this section. Note Importing your web server(s) into the Data Warehouse will not modify any of your other DomainMOD data, nor any of the data on your web server. Supported Data The following WHM sections are currently supported, but our end goal is to have every piece of WHM information that can be retrieved via the API stored in the Data Warehouse. Accounts Domain, IP Address, Owner, User, Contact Email, Plan, Theme, Shell, Partition, Disk Limit, Disk Usage, Max Addons, Max FTP Accounts, Max Email Lists, Max Parked Domains, Max POP Accounts, Max SQL Accounts, Max Subdomains, Creation Date, Suspend Status, Suspend Reason, Suspend Time, Max Email Per Hour, Failed Email % Before Defer, Min Failed Email # Before Defer DNS Zones Zone Filename, Original/Primary Source of Zone Data, Admin Email, Serial #, Refresh, Retry, Expiry, Minimum TTL, Authoritative Name Server DNS Records TTL, Class, Type, IP Address, CNAME, Mail Server, Mail Server Priority, TXT Data, Line # of Zone, # of Lines, RAW Data Setup In order to use the Data Warehouse you first need to add your web server(s). Note When adding your server you will be asked for either an API Token or a Remote Access Key/Hash, which can be found in your WHM (see below). The Remote Access Key/Hash will be getting removed from WHM in version 68 though, so if your WHM already supports the API Token that's what you should use. Adding A Web Server Navigate to Administration -> Data Warehouse . If the introduction page appears, click Proceed to the Data Warehouse . Click the Manage Servers button. Click the Add Web Server button. Enter your web server's details and then click the Add Server button. Note The Verify SSL Certificate? setting is on by default, and was switched on for existing servers when you upgraded to v4.24.02. Leave it on unless your server uses a self-signed certificate and you connect over a network you trust. When it's on, the server's SSL certificate must be valid for the host name you entered. If your server's certificate can't be verified, see Troubleshooting before switching it off. Retrieving Your Remote Access Key/Hash If your WHM server supports it, you should be using an API Token instead of the Remote Access Key/Hash. Skip to the next section to retrieve your API Token. Login to your WHM. Using the search box on the left-hand side of the screen, search for Remote Access Key . Click on Remote Access Key on the menu and your key will be displayed. Retrieving Your API Token Login to your WHM. Using the search box on the left-hand side of the screen, search for Manage API Tokens . Click on Manage API Tokens on the menu. Click the Generate Token button. Type in a name for your API Token and then click Generate . This name is used to help identify what that specific API Token was generated for, and you can call it anything you want. After you click the Generate button your API Token will be displayed. Building The Data Warehouse Once you've added your web server(s), building your Data Warehouse is just a couple clicks away. Navigate to Administration -> Data Warehouse . If the introduction page appears, click Proceed to the Data Warehouse . Click the Rebuild DW button. Once you confirm, DomainMOD will build the Data Warehouse, which may take some time. Depending on how much data you have stored on your web server, this process may time out. Instead of building the Data Warehouse manually like this, we recommend that you set up the cron job that comes with DomainMOD, which will completely automate your Data Warehouse builds.

docs.text: Encrypted Database Connections DomainMOD can encrypt its connection to your database with TLS, and check the database server's certificate so that nobody on the network can read or change your data along the way. If your database runs on the same server as DomainMOD (for example, $dbhostname is localhost ), the connection never crosses the network and you don't need to change anything. If your database is on a different server, or is reached over a network you don't fully trust, you should use the verify setting below. Settings The connection is controlled by two optional settings in _includes/config.inc.php . $dbsslmode 'auto' (the default) DomainMOD connects the same way it always has, and only uses an encrypted connection if the database server requires one. This encrypted connection doesn't check the server's certificate, so it doesn't protect you from an attacker on the network. 'verify' DomainMOD always encrypts the connection and checks the server's certificate. If the certificate can't be checked, DomainMOD won't connect. Use this whenever your database is on a different server than DomainMOD, or is reached over an untrusted network. 'off' DomainMOD never encrypts the connection. $dbsslca For 'verify' only, the path to the file containing the certificate of the Certificate Authority (CA) that signed your database server's certificate. If you leave it out, DomainMOD uses your system's trusted CA file: the one set by openssl.cafile in php.ini, then the SSL_CERT_FILE environment variable, then OpenSSL's default CA file. CA directories (such as openssl.capath ) aren't used, so if your trusted CAs are only in a directory, point $dbsslca at a CA file instead. Database providers that sign their certificates with their own CA, such as Amazon RDS, need their CA bundle saved on your server and $dbsslca pointed at it. For Amazon RDS, see Using SSL/TLS to encrypt a connection to a DB instance . Turning On Certificate Checking Make sure your database server has TLS enabled with a certificate. Make sure $dbhostname in _includes/config.inc.php matches the name on the database server's certificate. Add the following line to _includes/config.inc.php : $dbsslmode = 'verify'; If your database server's certificate is signed by its own CA rather than one in your system's trusted CA file, save the CA file on your server and add a line pointing at it: $dbsslca = '/path/to/ca.pem'; Load DomainMOD in your browser. If it can't connect, the error message will tell you that the certificate couldn't be checked. Check the two settings above, and that the CA file can be read by your web server. Checking the Connection You can see how DomainMOD is connected to your database by going to Administration -> System Information and looking at Database Connection . It will show one of the following: Encrypted (certificate checked) The connection is encrypted and the server's certificate was checked. This is what you want to see if your database is on a different server. Encrypted (certificate not checked) The connection is encrypted, but the server's certificate wasn't checked, so it isn't protected from an attacker on the network. Not encrypted The connection isn't encrypted.

docs.text: One of the easiest options for adding domains is to use the Domain Queue, which allows you to supply a list of domains and let DomainMOD take care of the rest (and in some cases you don't even need to supply the list of domains, it will be automatically retrieved from your registrar account). If your registrar has an API that DomainMOD supports, the Domain Queue uses it to retrieve the information required to add your domains, so before using this option make sure your API credentials have been saved with your registrar account. If your registrar isn't supported, you can still paste in a list of your domains, and DomainMOD will look up their details using RDAP, the public replacement for WHOIS, or WHOIS itself for domains that RDAP doesn't cover. Supported Registrars The following registrars are currently supported by the Domain Queue: Above.com, Cloudflare, DNSimple, DreamHost, Dynadot, eNom, Fabulous, Freenom (Reseller Accounts Only), Gandi, GoDaddy, Hostinger, Internet.bs, Name.com, NameBright, Namecheap, NameSilo, OpenSRS, OVH, Porkbun, ResellerClub, and SiteHost If your registrar isn't on this list, you can still use the Domain Queue by adding your domains without an API . Usage Requirement In order to use the Domain Queue you must first set up the cron job that comes with DomainMOD. Click on Domains on the main menu. Click Add Domains Automatically on the Domains page. Once you have domains, it's in the menu beside the Add Domain button. Click the Add Domains Using an API button. On the dropdown list, choose the registrar account that you would like to import using the Domain Queue, and click Next Step . If requested, paste in a list of the domains you want to add to the Domain Queue. This is not always required, as some domain registrars will retrieve the list of domains from your account automatically. Click the Add Domains button. You will now be taken to the Import Queue page, where you can see the status of your domain imports. You can also open it by clicking Import Queue on the main menu (this menu option is only shown while the Domain Queue or the SSL Queue has entries). As of v4.27.0, the page also shows the SSL Queue . Once all of your imports have completed you can click the Clear Completed button in order to clear the queue. Adding Domains Without an API If DomainMOD doesn't support your registrar's API, you can paste in a list of your domains and DomainMOD will look up each one using RDAP, the public replacement for WHOIS, or WHOIS itself for domains that RDAP doesn't cover. This fills in each domain's expiry date and DNS servers, and works out which registrar it's at, so you don't need to choose a registrar or enter any API details. Click on Domains on the main menu. Click Add Domains Automatically on the Domains page. Once you have domains, it's in the menu beside the Add Domain button. If you haven't added a registrar and a registrar account yet, it can add them for you. Click the Add Domains Without an API button. Choose the owner of the domains. Paste in your list of domains, one per line (up to 1,000 at a time). Click the Add Domains button, and you'll be taken to the Import Queue page, where you can follow the progress of your imports. A registrar that isn't in DomainMOD yet is added for you. Each domain goes into your account at that registrar if you have exactly one, or otherwise into a general account named "RDAP Import", which is created the first time it's needed and used for later imports. Note Neither RDAP nor WHOIS includes a domain's WHOIS privacy or auto-renewal status, so both are set to No. You can update them afterwards using the Bulk Updater . Some country-code registries (such as .de, .nl, and .au) don't publish expiry dates, so those domains can't be looked up this way. WHOIS lookups also need your server to be able to connect to WHOIS servers on port 43, which some web hosts block. If a domain can't be looked up, it fails in the queue with the reason, and you can finish it by hand with Fix and Import . Fixing Failed Domains If a domain fails in the Domain Queue, you can fix it by hand and import it, rather than adding it again from scratch. On the Domain Queue page, click the edit icon ( Fix and Import ) beside the domain that failed. The Fix and Import page shows the reason the domain failed, and is pre-filled with everything the Domain Queue already knows about it. Fill in the rest of its details, such as the expiry date and registrar account. Click the Import Domain button. The domain is added with the creation type "Queue (Edited Manually)", and the Domain Queue shows it as "Imported (Edited Manually)". Keeping Domains Up To Date Once your domains have been added, you can update a single domain at any time using the Refresh button on its edit page. See Refreshing Domains for details. API Notes This section contains various notes and things to watch out for when using the domain registrar APIs. Cloudflare A Cloudflare registrar account uses the following fields: Username : your Cloudflare account email address. This is required if you use a Global API Key. If you use an API Token it can be any name for the account. Account ID : shown on your Cloudflare dashboard. API Key : either an API Token (recommended) or your Global API Key. An API Token needs read access to Registrar domains, plus Zone Read access so that DomainMOD can retrieve the domains' name servers. DreamHost DreamHost does not currently allow the WHOIS privacy status of a domain to be retrieved via their API, so all domains added to the Domain Queue from a DreamHost account will have their WHOIS privacy status set to No by default. Dynadot You'll find the API Key and API Secret under Tools -> API in your Dynadot account. As of v4.27.0, a registrar account with an API Secret uses Dynadot's current API. Without one, DomainMOD uses Dynadot's legacy API, which Dynadot plans to retire, so add the API Secret soon. The same API Key works for both. If you restrict API access by IP address at Dynadot, add your server's IP address to the allowed list. Freenom Freenom currently only gives API access to reseller accounts. Gandi For the API Key, create a personal access token in your Gandi account with read access to your domains. Older Gandi API keys still work. Gandi does not currently allow the WHOIS privacy status of a domain to be retrieved via their API, so all domains added to the Domain Queue from a Gandi account will have their WHOIS privacy status set to No by default. GoDaddy For the API Key, create a Personal Access Token at https://developer.godaddy.com/personal-access-token with the domains.domain:read permission, and leave the API Secret blank. A classic API key and secret also still work until GoDaddy retires them. When retrieving your list of domains from GoDaddy, the current limit is 1,000 domains. If you have more than this you should export the full list of domains from GoDaddy and paste it into the Domains to add field when adding domains via the Domain Queue. GoDaddy only gives API access to accounts it considers eligible, and has at times limited it to accounts with at least 10 domains or a Discount Domain Club membership. If GoDaddy refuses your account's API requests, domains added to the Domain Queue from it will stay at "Pending". Hostinger For the API Key, create an API token in your Hostinger dashboard ( Dev tools -> API -> API tokens ). Hostinger API tokens have full access to your Hostinger account, so consider giving the token an expiry date. Hostinger does not return the Auto-Renewal status when retrieving the details of a domain, so all domains imported via the API will have their Auto-Renewal status set to No by default. NameSilo NameSilo's domains have 6 possible statuses: Active, Expired (grace period), Expired (restore period), Expired (pending delete), Inactive, and Pending Outbound Transfer When retrieving your list of domains via the API, Inactive domains are not returned. When retrieving the details of a specific domain via the API, Inactive and Expired (pending delete) domains will not return any data. OVH An OVH registrar account uses the following fields: API Key : your OVH Application Key. API Secret : your Application Secret. Account ID : your Consumer Key. Create all three on the key page for your OVH region ( Europe , Canada , or US ), with two read-only rights: GET /domain and GET /domain/* . Porkbun When retrieving your list of domains from Porkbun, the current limit is 1,000 domains. If you have more than this you should export the full list of domains from Porkbun and paste it into the Domains to add field when adding domains via the Domain Queue. ResellerClub ResellerClub does not allow users to retrieve a list of their domains via the API, nor does it return the Auto-Renewal status when retrieving the details of a domain. All domains imported via the API will have their Auto-Renewal status set to No by default. SiteHost A SiteHost registrar account uses the following fields: Account ID : your SiteHost Account ID, which is shown on your SiteHost invoices. API Key : a key from the SiteHost Control Panel (in the API module) with access to Domains (SRS) . SiteHost prices are in NZD. Example Below is an example of how to use the Domain Queue to import the domains from a Namecheap account: Create a Domain Registrar asset, ensuring that you've selected Namecheap on the API Support dropdown list. Create an IP Address asset, ensuring that you enter the public IP address that DomainMOD's server uses for outgoing connections (usually the server's own public IP address, unless its traffic goes out through another address). Create a Domain Registrar Account asset, ensuring that you've entered your account username and API Key, and that you've selected the IP address that you created in the previous step. On your Namecheap account, go to Profile -> Tools to view the status of your API access. Next, click on Manage to view your whitelisted IP addresses. If your API Access was not enabled in the previous step, you can enable it here. To the right of the Whitelisted IPs section, click on Edit to view your whitelisted IP addresses. On the Whitelisted IPs page, ensure that your public IP address is listed. And that's it, your Namecheap API connection should now be set up! With your API connection up and running, it's time to import your domains using the Domain Queue .

docs.text: Installation Which PHP database extensions does DomainMOD need? DomainMOD needs both the PDO extension with its MariaDB/MySQL driver ( pdo_mysql ), which it uses for everyday work, and the MySQLi extension ( mysqli ), which it uses to restore a database backup. The old MySQL extension isn't supported. If the installer or the System Information page says either one is disabled, install and enable that module on your server. Configuration Can I import my domains into DomainMOD using a CSV file? Yes. As of v4.19, you can use the CSV Importer to import all of your domain data using a CSV template. You can also use the Domain Queue to import your domains automatically, either using your registrar's API (if it's supported by DomainMOD ) or by adding them without an API . Does DomainMOD support multiple languages? Yes! As of v4.16.0 DomainMOD supports Arabic, Bengali, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Dutch, English (CA), English (US), French, German, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Marathi, Persian, Polish, Portuguese, Portuguese (BR), Russian, Spanish, Tamil, Telugu, Turkish, Urdu, and Vietnamese. If you speak one of these languages, you will probably be horrified at the quality of the current translations. This is because an automated translation service was used for this, but I hope the quality of the translations will improve greatly over time. If you would like to help improve the translations, feel free to head over to our translations page on GitHub . Which domain registrar APIs does DomainMOD currently support? DomainMOD currently supports Above.com, Cloudflare, DNSimple, DreamHost, Dynadot, eNom, Fabulous, Freenom (Reseller Accounts Only), Gandi, GoDaddy, Hostinger, Internet.bs, Name.com, NameBright, Namecheap, NameSilo, OpenSRS, OVH, Porkbun, ResellerClub, and SiteHost. If your registrar isn't supported, you can still import your domains with the Domain Queue by adding them without an API , which looks up their details using RDAP or WHOIS. Usage How many domains can I manage with DomainMOD? There's no set limit on the number of domains you can manage. It depends on your server hardware. As of v4.26.0, the Domains and SSL Certificates lists (and, as of v4.27.0, the Hosting list) load from the server one page at a time (up to 500 rows a page), and sort and search on the server too, so they stay quick even with tens of thousands of domains. Can I use DomainMOD to sell domains? The primary use for DomainMOD is to manage a large portfolio of domains, and it currently doesn't have any sales features, such as being able to host sales letter landing pages. This is something we're looking at implementing in a future version of DomainMOD. If all you want to do is track the amount you sold a domain for, you can create a Custom Field, which will allow you to record the sales amount for your domains. I don't need to keep track of the fees associated with my domains. Can I disable this feature? There's currently no way to disable fees, as the system requires them in order to link the database tables, but if you don't care about keeping track of the fees you can just enter zeros for all of the costs. I noticed you can set the registration, transfer, and renewal prices for domains via their domain registrars, but can you set a purchase price for a specific domain? For example, if I purchase a domain from a 3rd party marketplace can I record this information in DomainMOD? Although this is not a standard field, you can use Custom Fields to keep track of the purchase price of your domains. Is it possible to display the custom fields I've created on the main domain page as a column? Yes. As of v4.13, you can choose which custom fields to show as columns in Settings -> Display Settings , and the same goes for the SSL Certificates page (and, as of v4.27.0, the Hosting page). Are the domain expiration dates updated automatically? Yes, as of v4.27.0, once an administrator enables the Refresh Domains task in the Task Scheduler. You can also refresh a single domain whenever you like by clicking the Refresh button on its edit page. See Refreshing Domains for details. Expiration dates can also be updated one-by-one by editing the domain, or by using the Bulk Updater . Does DomainMOD support internationalized domain names (IDNs)? Yes. As of v4.25.0, you can enter an internationalized domain name such as münchen.de in either its Unicode form or its punycode form (xn--mnchen-3ya.de), and DomainMOD stores it in its lowercase Unicode form, so searches match it whichever form you use. The one exception is a name with a character that the database can't store, such as an emoji, which is kept in punycode. This works everywhere you add domains, including the CSV Importer, the Bulk Updater, and the Domain Queue, and DomainMOD converts the domain back to punycode when it talks to registrar APIs and other servers. When you upgrade to v4.25.0, any domains you've already stored in punycode are converted to Unicode (apart from the exception above). If this leaves two domains with the same name (for example, münchen.de and xn--mnchen-3ya.de), both are kept so that you can decide which one to keep. Do you plan to add API support for domain registries? For API imports we've been trying to focus on actual registrars, since unlike registries they cover more than just one (or a few) domain extensions, and actual registrars are what most domainers use, which is who DomainMOD is primarily for. There are always exceptions to this of course, but in general this is the case. Also, if we were to start adding API import support for registries this would open up a pretty big can of worms, since there are literally hundreds of registries that could be added. If we add one registrar we add support for all of the extensions that registrar has, whereas if we add support for a registry we only add support for a single extension (or in some cases a few extensions). docs.text: If you've just finished installing DomainMOD and are wondering how to start using it, this section is for you. We'll walk you through the first few steps you need to take with a new installation, and after completing the steps below you'll be ready to start adding your domains. If you haven't installed DomainMOD yet, please see the Getting Started section. Login The first thing you need to do is log in to your new DomainMOD installation using the administrator username and password you chose during installation. The admin account that gets created during installation has full control of your DomainMOD installation, so you should store the password in a safe place. docs.text: Project Home: https://domainmod.org Project Demo: https://demo.domainmod.org Documentation: https://domainmod.org/docs/ Support: https://domainmod.org/support/ Source Code: https://domainmod.org/source/ About DomainMOD is a free, open source, self-hosted application for managing your domains, hosting services, SSL certificates, and other internet assets in one place. DomainMOD also includes a Data Warehouse framework that allows you to import your web server data so that you can view, export, and report on your live data. Currently the Data Warehouse only supports web servers running WHM/cPanel. Live Demo Not sure if DomainMOD is what you're looking for? Don't want to take the time to install it only to find out that it's not? We hate when that happens ourselves, which is why we've set up a live demo so you don't waste your time. So go ahead, take the live demo for a test drive before you install: https://demo.domainmod.org Requirements Software : PHP 8.2-8.5, MariaDB 10.4-12.3 or MySQL 5.7-9.7 PHP Extensions : PDO (MariaDB/MySQL), cURL, OpenSSL, gettext, MySQLi PHP Settings : allow_url_fopen Folders : the web server can write to the 'temp' folder Downloading There are currently four options for downloading DomainMOD. Option #1 -- Using Docker Please see our official DomainMOD container on Docker Hub for more information: https://hub.docker.com/r/domainmod/domainmod Option #2 -- Downloading a .zip file Visit the following URL to download DomainMOD in a .zip file: https://domainmod.org/download/ Option #3 -- Using Git To download using Git, change to the directory that will hold DomainMOD and run the following command, which puts it in a new domainmod folder there (this download option requires that you have Git installed on your server): git clone https://github.com/domainmod/domainmod.git Option #4 -- Installing via Softaculous Softaculous is the web hosting industry's leading software auto-installer, and it has helped millions of users install applications with a few clicks of a mouse. Softaculous easily integrates into the leading control panels like cPanel, Plesk, DirectAdmin, InterWorx, H-Sphere, and more. Check your hosting control panel or contact your web host if you're not sure if they offer Softaculous. To install DomainMOD simply open Softaculous, use the search feature to find DomainMOD, and then click the "Install Now" button. After you answer a few questions about your installation Softaculous will do the rest. More Information: http://www.softaculous.com/softaculous/apps/others/DomainMOD/ Installing If you installed DomainMOD using Docker or Softaculous in the previous step you can ignore the rest of this Installing section, as you should already have DomainMOD up-and-running. If you downloaded the .zip file in the previous step, you will now need to upload the archive to your web server and then unpack it into the folder where you wish to install (or unpack it and then upload it, whichever you prefer). If you used Git to retrieve the source code in the previous step, just change to the directory where you ran the git command and your files are already waiting for you in a folder called /domainmod/. Feel free to rename this folder to whatever you want. Installation Steps Create a MySQL database that will be used to store DomainMOD's data. In the '_includes' folder, copy config.SAMPLE.inc.php to config.inc.php and then update config.inc.php to reflect your web server's settings (including the recommended $secret_key for MFA). Make sure the web server can write to the 'temp' folder and the files in it, or restores are turned off. If your cron job runs as a different user, give both users write access to the folder. In a web browser, visit the URL where you installed DomainMOD (for example, example.com/domainmod/) and work through the installer. When it's done, you'll be taken to the sign-in page. Set up the cron job below on your web server. The Secret Key $secret_key is a long random value that DomainMOD uses to encrypt each user's MFA secret. It's best to set it when you install, before anyone turns on MFA. See Security and MFA for details. The 'temp' Folder DomainMOD keeps its restore lock and its lookup caches in the 'temp' folder, and restores are turned off until the web server can write to the folder and its restore.lock file. For example, if your web server runs PHP as www-data, run sudo chown -R www-data temp from the folder you installed DomainMOD in, and set up the cron job to run as www-data too. The Installer On Administrator Account , choose the username and password you'll sign in with. The password needs at least 8 characters and no more than 72 bytes: letters, numbers, and symbols on a standard English keyboard take one byte each, and characters such as é take more. On Ready to Install , check your choices and click Install DomainMOD . Cron Job DomainMOD includes a Task Scheduler that allows you to run various system jobs at specified times, which helps keep your DomainMOD installation up-to-date and running smoothly, as well as notifies you of important information, such as emailing you to let you know about upcoming domain, hosting service, and SSL certificate renewals. The Task Scheduler is very powerful, and it enables features that you otherwise wouldn't be able to use, but in order for it to function you need to schedule the below cron job to run on your web server. Once the cron job is set up to run, the Task Scheduler will be live. If you installed DomainMOD using Docker, the cron job will be set up and running automatically within the container, so there's nothing you need to set up manually. Filename: /cron.php Note This file should be executed every 10 minutes. If your cron job runs cron.php from the command line, the simplest setup is to run it as the same user PHP runs as for your web server, so both can write to DomainMOD's 'temp' folder. Task Scheduler Key (Optional) By default, cron.php runs whenever its URL is opened, which is how many installations schedule it. As of v4.25.0, you can stop anyone else from running it by giving it a key. Add the following line to your config.inc.php file, replacing YourKeyHere with a long, random value: $cron_key = 'YourKeyHere'; Once a key is set, cron.php only runs from the command line ( php cron.php ) or from a URL that includes the key, such as https://example.com/cron.php?key=YourKeyHere , so update your cron job to match. If cron.php is opened without the right key, it displays "This script needs its key" and doesn't run any tasks. Security Although we've done our best to secure DomainMOD, unfortunately there are many factors that could cause security holes, such as the software being run on insecure hardware, software like PHP and MySQL having out-of-date versions with known vulnerabilities, easy-to-guess passwords being used, and so on. Due to these factors we recommend the following steps to help secure your DomainMOD installation. Secure your installation with an SSL Certificate. If your database is on a different server than DomainMOD, encrypt the connection and check the server's certificate by adding $dbsslmode = 'verify'; to config.inc.php. See Encrypted Database Connections for details. Do not use easy-to-guess passwords. Ever . Although DomainMOD has its own authentication system, we recommend that you also use HTTP authentication on your installation directory to add an extra layer of security. Do not store your account passwords or API keys in DomainMOD. Although the ability to save this information exists, use it at your own risk . This information is fairly secure if you run DomainMOD on your local computer, but there's a much higher risk of someone gaining access to it if you host the site on a server that is accessible to the outside world. Warning Saving your API keys (and other relevant API connection information) in DomainMOD is necessary if you want to use your registrar's API to import domains through the Domain Queue or to refresh them (the Refresh button and the Refresh Domains task). Imports and refreshes using RDAP and WHOIS don't need them, but they can't read WHOIS privacy or auto renewal. If you don't need those, we recommend that you only save this information while you're using the Domain Queue, and that you remove it as soon as you're done. Do not host DomainMOD on a public website or on an easy-to-guess URL. If you do end up hosting DomainMOD on a public website, DomainMOD asks search engines not to index its pages. Don't block its URL in your website's robots.txt file, since search engines then can't see that request, and your DomainMOD URL may still end up in public search results. Do not give the URL to anyone who does not need to access DomainMOD. You should treat the URL like a password. Always use the most up-to-date version of DomainMOD. This will help protect you from any security vulnerabilities that are found and fixed. Turn on multi-factor authentication (MFA) for your account, and consider requiring it for every user. See Security and MFA for details. First Run After you've installed DomainMOD you should go through the First Run section to finish getting the software ready to use.

docs.text: As of v4.27.0, DomainMOD keeps track of your hosting services, such as web hosting plans, servers, and email hosting, alongside your domains and SSL certificates. Each service belongs to a hosting account at a hosting provider, has a service type and a billing term, and gets its cost from a hosting fee. Your domains can each be linked to the service they use. Getting Set Up Before adding a service, add the hosting provider and your account there (see Creating Assets ). DomainMOD comes with a set of service types (Cloud, Dedicated, DNS, Email, Other, Reseller, Shared, and VPS), and you can add your own under Assets -> Hosting Service Types . Types are shared by every provider. A fee is set per provider, service type, and billing term, so if one provider sells two shared plans at different prices, add a type for each (such as Shared Starter and Shared Pro). Adding a Hosting Service Click Hosting on the main menu. Click the Add Hosting Service button. Enter the service's Name , and choose its Hosting Account (the owner comes from the account), Service Type , Billing Term (1, 3, 6, 12, 24, or 36 months), and Status . Enter the Renewal Date , and choose whether Auto-Renewal is on. Renews On Day is the day of the month it renews on, so if a shorter month moves a renewal earlier, the next one goes back to that day. Under Where It Runs , you can enter the Hostname and choose an IP Address . Choose a Category , and add any Notes . Click the Add Hosting Service button. Fees A service's cost comes from the hosting fee that matches its provider, service type, and billing term. To add one, click Assets on the main menu, click Hosting Providers under Hosting , then click Fees beside the provider, and click Add Fee . A fee has an Initial Fee (for your records, and not counted in costs), a Renewal Fee for each billing term, and an optional Misc Fee that's added to every renewal, such as a control panel license. When you add or change a fee, the services that match it are updated. A service with no matching fee is saved without a cost and shows No fee in the list, and it's left out of cost totals until you add one. Reporting -> Hosting Fees lists the fees that are missing. The Hosting list's Yearly Cost is each service's cost per billing term scaled to 12 months. The Hosting Page The Hosting page lists your live hosting services (Active and Pending) to start with. You can filter it by Hosting Provider , Hosting Account , Service Type , Billing Term , IP Address , Category , Owner , and Status , and by renewal date. Export downloads the list as a CSV file, and you can choose its columns in Settings -> Display Settings . Click a service to open its page, where you can edit its details and see its Change History . Its Domains section lists the domains that use it, each with its expiry date and status. Linking Domains A domain's add and edit pages have a Hosting Service menu, under Hosting . Choose a service, or None . Choosing a service also fills in the domain's IP Address with the service's (on a domain you're editing, only if its IP address isn't already set), which you can still change, since a domain can point somewhere else (such as through a proxy). To link many domains at once, use the Bulk Updater 's Change Hosting Service action. The Domains list can show a Hosting Service column, and its Hosting Service filter finds the domains on a service, or with none. Renewals When a service renews, open it and click Mark Renewed , which moves its renewal date forward one billing term. Once a service's renewal date has passed, it shows one of these: Confirm renewal : the service is Active and auto-renew is on, so the host should have renewed it. Check that it did, then choose Mark Renewed . After 14 days, it shows as overdue. Overdue : auto-renew is off, the service is Pending, or it waited more than 14 days for confirmation. Hosting services are included in the expiration email, the Dashboard, the Renewal Calendar, and the reports , including Hosting Renewals and At-Risk Hosting Services . Cancelled Services To stop tracking a service you no longer have, set its Status to Cancelled . A cancelled service is hidden from the list unless you filter by status, has no renewals, and is left out of costs. Domains already linked to it keep the link, but it can't be chosen for other domains. A service can be deleted from the bottom of its page, and any linked domains are kept without a hosting service. Hosting providers, accounts, and service types can only be deleted once nothing uses them. Custom Hosting Fields Administrators can add custom fields for hosting services in Administration -> Custom Hosting Fields . See Custom Fields .

docs.text: Warning Before migrating it's strongly recommended that you backup your DomainMOD installation directory and database. If something goes wrong during the migration process there may be no way to recover your data, and having a backup of your installation directory and database will allow you to easily restore your data. The Backup & Restore instructions can be found here . To migrate your DomainMOD installation from one server to another: [Old Server] Upgrade to the newest version of DomainMOD [Old Server] Export a copy of your DomainMOD database using the above Backup feature [New Server] Download and install the newest version of DomainMOD [New Server] Login to DomainMOD and navigate to Administration -> Backup & Restore [New Server] In the Restore section, click the Choose File button and then select the domainmod-backup.sql file that you want to restore [New Server] Click the Restore Entire Database button [New Server] Once the restore is complete you will automatically be logged out of DomainMOD. You should now be able to login using the accounts that you just restored. That's it! DomainMOD has now been migrated to your new server.

docs.text: DomainMOD can look up a domain's current details and update them for you, either when you click Refresh on the domain's edit page (as of v4.25.0), or automatically with the Refresh Domains task (as of v4.27.0). The changes a refresh makes are recorded in the Change History . Refresh On the domain's edit page, click the Refresh button near the top, and DomainMOD will look up the domain's current details and update them straight away, listing what changed. If your registrar account uses a supported registrar API with its API details filled in, DomainMOD uses the API, which can update the expiry date, DNS servers, WHOIS privacy, and auto-renewal status (some registrars' APIs don't report all of these, and anything not reported is left as it is). Otherwise, or if the API can't be used, DomainMOD uses public RDAP and WHOIS data instead, which updates the expiry date and DNS servers, but not WHOIS privacy or auto-renewal. As of v4.27.0, Refresh also checks the transfer lock and registry status using RDAP where it's available, whichever source updates the other details, and looks up the domain's live DNS . To avoid overloading your registrar and the RDAP and WHOIS servers, there's a short wait between refreshes. If you've changed the expiry date, DNS servers, WHOIS privacy, auto-renewal, or notes without saving, DomainMOD asks before a refresh replaces your changes. Read-only users don't see the Refresh button. Automatic Refreshes The Refresh Domains task refreshes your live domains (every domain that isn't Expired or Sold) a few at a time, the same way Refresh does, and records its changes in the Change History as Scheduled Refresh. It's off by default, so an administrator needs to enable it in Administration -> Task Scheduler , and the cron job must be set up (Docker installs already run it). See Task Scheduler for how it checks each domain. Each live domain's Change History section shows its automatic check status, such as when it was last checked and when its next check is due. Registry Status and Transfer Lock As of v4.27.0, Refresh reads each domain's registry status codes from RDAP, along with its transfer lock: Locked , Not Locked , Unknown (the registry didn't report a clear status, or RDAP isn't available for the TLD), Couldn't Check (no status could be read yet), or Not Checked . Domains added with the Domain Queue's RDAP import get them too. Some country-code registries don't use transfer locks. The domain's edit page has a Registry Status section, the Domains list has a Registry Status filter, and you can add a Transfer Lock column in Settings -> Display Settings . A domain that the registry has on hold, or is deleting or restoring, gets an On Hold , Being Deleted , or Being Restored badge. For live domains expiring in the next 30 days, or already past their expiry date, the At-Risk Domains report (and the Dashboard's at-risk count) also covers ones with the transfer lock off ( Transfer Lock Off , for domains not yet expired) and ones on hold or being deleted or restored ( Registry Hold or Deletion ). Live DNS As of v4.27.0, after each refresh (clicked or automatic), when there's time left, DomainMOD looks up the domain's live name servers, IP addresses (for the domain and its www name), and mail servers. These lookups go through your server's own DNS resolver, so whoever runs that resolver can see the names being checked. DomainMOD compares the live name servers with the domain's DNS profile, and the live addresses with its IP Address. Live DNS only reports what it finds. It never changes the domain, its DNS profile, or its IP Address. The Live DNS section on the domain's edit page shows what was found and how it compares. When one of your DNS profiles or IP Addresses matches what's live, Use it picks it in the edit form (click Save to keep it), and Add this IP Address opens the Add IP Address form with a live address that isn't in DomainMOD yet filled in. Changes to the live name servers and addresses are recorded in the Change History. On the Domains list, you can add a Live DNS column in Settings -> Display Settings , and use the Live DNS filter to find domains whose name servers or IP address differ, that have no DNS, or whose check failed or hasn't run. The Domains export includes it too.

docs.text: As of v4.27.0, DomainMOD supports multi-factor authentication (MFA): after your password, you enter a six-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone, so someone who learns your password still can't sign in. The Security Page Navigate to Settings -> Security . You can also open it from the menu under your name in the top bar, which shows whether MFA is on for your account. The Security page replaces the old Change Password page. It's where you: change your password (your current password is now required) turn MFA on or off see how many recovery codes you have left, and regenerate them forget the devices you chose to remember Turning On MFA On the Security page, click Turn On MFA . If you're asked for your password, enter it and click Continue . Scan the QR code with your authenticator app, or type the key into it, then enter the six-digit code it shows and click Turn On MFA . Save the ten recovery codes that are shown, using Copy or Download , somewhere safe such as a password manager. They aren't shown again. Click I've Saved These Codes . From then on, DomainMOD asks for a code each time you sign in. When you reach DomainMOD over HTTPS, you can tick Remember This Device for 30 Days to skip the code on that device for 30 days. If you don't have your phone, click Use a Recovery Code . Each recovery code works once, and after signing in with one you can set up a new authenticator on the Security page. Note The codes depend on the time, so your server's clock needs to be correct. If a code is refused during setup because the clock is a few minutes off, DomainMOD may say so. Forgotten Passwords On the sign-in page, click Forgot your password? , enter your username or email address, and click Reset Password . As of v4.24.0, DomainMOD emails you a link that works once and expires after an hour. Open it and click Reset Password , and a new password is emailed to you. For Administrators Requiring MFA: In Administration -> System Settings , under Set Up MFA , turn on Require MFA for All Users , then click Update MFA Setting . You need MFA on for your own account first. Users who don't have it on are signed out, and until they set it up, they can only change their password and set up MFA. Resetting a user's MFA: If a user loses their authenticator app and their recovery codes, open Administration -> Users , edit the user, tick Reset this user's MFA , and click Reset MFA . Their other sessions are signed out, and they set it up again at their next sign-in (or under Settings if MFA isn't required). Another administrator can't reset the account with the username admin, so keep its recovery codes especially safe. The Users list shows who has MFA on, and users are emailed when their MFA is turned on, turned off, or reset. Encrypting MFA secrets: By default, each user's MFA secret is stored in the database without encryption, so a database backup includes it. To encrypt them, set $secret_key in /_includes/config.inc.php to a long random value ( openssl rand -hex 32 or php -r 'echo bin2hex(random_bytes(32)), "\n";' makes one), ideally when you install, before anyone turns on MFA, as described in config.SAMPLE.inc.php (Docker installs use the DOMAINMOD_SECRET_KEY variable). Secrets saved before the key was set are encrypted the next time each user signs in with a code from their authenticator app. The key isn't in DomainMOD's backups, so keep it safe and use the same value when you move or restore your installation. If it's lost or changed, users with MFA on need a recovery code or an administrator's reset to sign in. Set Up MFA shows whether a key is set.

docs.text: Segments are saved lists of domains that you can filter the Domains list by, such as the domains used by one client or project, or a list you've been sent to check. The domains don't have to be in DomainMOD, so a segment also shows you which ones are missing. Adding a Segment Click Segments on the main menu. Click the Add Segment button. Enter a Segment Name (up to 35 characters), and paste in the Segment Domains , one per line. Add a Description and any Notes , if you'd like. Click the Add Segment button. If any of the domains aren't valid, DomainMOD lists them so you can fix them, and the segment isn't saved until they're fixed. Editing a Segment On the Segments page, click a segment's name to change its name, domains, description, or notes, then click Save . To delete a segment, click Delete this segment in the Danger Zone at the bottom of the page. Deleting a segment doesn't affect the domains in it. Filtering the Domains List On the Domains page, click Filters , choose a segment from the Segment menu, and click Apply filters . The list then shows only the domains in the segment, and you can use the other filters with it, such as Registrar or Status . A summary above the list shows: Domains in Segment : how many domains the segment has Matching Domains : how many of them are on the list, and their Total Cost Matching But Inactive Domains : domains that are in DomainMOD but are Expired or Sold Matching But Filtered Domains : active domains that the list's other filters leave out Missing Domains : domains that aren't in DomainMOD at all The last three are only shown when they have any domains, and each one's View link lists them, with an Export Results button that downloads them as a CSV file. The segment is shown above the list with the other filters in use, where you can remove it. Exporting On the Segments page, the Export button downloads every segment and its domains as a CSV file, and the Export link beside a segment downloads just that one. On the Domains page, Export downloads the domains the list is showing, with the segment's summary at the top.
