docs.text: As of v4.27.0, the SSL Queue imports your SSL certificates for you. Paste a list of hostnames, and DomainMOD connects to each site, reads the certificate it serves, and adds it as an SSL certificate with its expiry date and issuer. New certificates are linked to their domain when DomainMOD has just one record of that domain. Requirement The SSL Queue is processed by the SSL Queue Processing task, so you must set up the cron job that comes with DomainMOD (Docker installs already run it). Adding SSL Certificates Automatically Click SSL Certificates on the main menu. Choose Add SSL Certificates Automatically from the menu beside the Add SSL Certificate button. Before you have any SSL certificates, it's a button on the page instead. Paste in up to 1,000 hostnames, one per line. Each line can be a hostname, such as example.com, or an https:// address. Choose the SSL Provider Account . Match each certificate's issuer (recommended) finds or adds the SSL provider for each certificate's issuer, and uses your account there, or adds an account named "SSL Import". Then choose the Owner (used with issuer matching, since a chosen account has its own owner), and, under Defaults for New Certificates , the Certificate Type , IP Address , and Category . The Owner , IP Address , and Category start on Same as the Domain , which gives each certificate its domain's values, or your SSL defaults for a hostname whose domain isn't in DomainMOD. Click the Add SSL Certificates button, and you'll be taken to the Import Queue page, where you can follow the progress of your imports. Only port 443 is checked, and only public sites can be reached. A hostname whose domain is still in the Domain Queue waits up to 7 days for it, and is then checked anyway. A certificate that's already in DomainMOD isn't added again: that's a live certificate with the same hostname, or the very same certificate. An expired record with the same hostname doesn't stop the new certificate being added. To update an existing certificate's expiry date, use Refresh on its edit page (see below). You can also import certificates while you add domains: when you add domains with the Domain Queue , Also import each domain's SSL certificate (on by default) adds each domain's site to the SSL Queue. Only the domains you paste are looked up, not the ones a registrar's API supplies. The Import Queue The Import Queue page shows the Domain Queue and the SSL Queue, one after the other, each with its own buttons. While either queue has entries, you can open it with Import Queue on the main menu. For each hostname, the SSL Queue shows its status, such as Pending , Processing , Retrying , Waiting for the Domain , Imported , or Failed , with the reason when there is one. An imported certificate that has expired or isn't trusted gets an Expired or Not trusted badge. A hostname is tried up to three times before it fails. Use Retry Failed to put failed hostnames back in the queue (a hostname whose chosen account or other setting has since been deleted has to be added again instead), Clear Completed to remove the finished ones, and Export to download the list. Note A new certificate needs a fee for its SSL provider and type, like any other SSL certificate. Until the fee is added, it's hidden from the SSL Certificates list (see Missing Fees in Assets -> SSL Fees ). Adding an SSL Certificate Manually First add an SSL provider and an SSL provider account , if you haven't already. Then click SSL Certificates on the main menu, and click the Add SSL Certificate button. Enter the certificate's Host / Label , such as example.com, and fill in its details. As of v4.27.0, a certificate doesn't need a domain: set Domain to None for one that isn't for a domain in DomainMOD. When you delete a domain, its SSL certificates are kept without a domain. Refreshing an SSL Certificate As of v4.27.0, an SSL certificate's edit page has a Refresh button near the top. It reads the certificate the site serves now, and updates the expiry date and status when they've changed, with a note saying what changed. A pending status is kept, and the SSL provider, account, type, and fee aren't changed. Refresh needs the certificate's Host / Label to be the hostname it's installed on, such as example.com, and part of the certificate's domain, if it has one.

docs.text: Installation The database tables are being created but some of the data isn't getting inserted I get a blank page and can't go any further I get an "Error 500" message MySQL strict mode may be enabled on your server. In order for DomainMOD to install and run, strict mode must to be disabled. To disable strict mode you need to edit your MySQL configuration file. In it there will be a line that looks like: sql-mode="STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION" To disable strict mode you need to remove STRICT_TRANS_TABLES from this line (including the comma after it, if there is one), which in this example would leave you with: sql-mode="NO_AUTO_CREATE_USER,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION" Once disabled you will need to restart MySQL, and then DomainMOD should install properly. Note As of v4.11, DomainMOD will try to disable strict mode automatically during the database connection, but if you're still experiencing issues you should follow the steps above. I'm receiving an error that there are too many redirects The images and CSS are broken This is generally caused by an invalid web root in your config.inc.php file. Please double check your config.inc.php file and confirm that the $web_root variable reflects the directory where you installed DomainMOD. For example, if you access DomainMOD via the URL http://example.com/domains/ the $web_root variable should be: $web_root = "/domains"; (don't include a trailing slash!) And if you've installed DomainMOD in the root folder of a domain or subdomain, the $web_root variable in your config.inc.php file should be blank, like so: $web_root = ""; Upgrading There was an issue while upgrading and now I can't access DomainMOD Although we personally haven't seen this happen yet, it's definitely possible. This is why we recommend you back up your DomainMOD installation directory and database before upgrading (you did make that backup, right?). Follow these steps to restore your copy of DomainMOD: Restore your DomainMOD database backup to the same location as your previous DomainMOD database. Instead of logging into DomainMOD to upgrade your database, run the below script from the command line. [FULL SERVER PATH TO DOMAINMOD]/update.php The full command will look something like this, depending on the location of PHP and DomainMOD on your server: /usr/bin/php -f /home/user/www/domainmod/update.php If you receive a notice that your upgrade was successful , switch back to your web browser and try to log in to DomainMOD. If you're able to log in successfully, you can ignore the rest of these steps. If you receive a notice that your upgrade was unsuccessful , keep a record of any error messages that are displayed and proceed to the next step. Restore your DomainMOD database backup again, then download the previous version that you were using and go through the standard installation steps, pointing it at your newly-restored database in the config.inc.php file. This should get you back to where you were before you tried upgrading. Contact us with any error messages that were displayed and we'll try to help figure out what went wrong with your upgrade. Usage The software seems to be working properly, but some messages are being displayed, such as " undefined index " and " undefined variable " This is related to the error reporting level that you have turned on in PHP. Although these are only warnings and won't actually be breaking anything, you can get rid of them by editing your php.ini file and changing the error_reporting line. Right now you probably have something that looks like this: error_reporting = E_ALL But you should have something that looks like this: error_reporting = E_ALL & ~E_NOTICE & ~E_DEPRECATED If your current line includes ~E_STRICT , you can remove it. PHP 8 never raises E_STRICT, and PHP 8.4 deprecated the constant. Commented out in your php.ini file, above the error_reporting directive, there may be a suggested error reporting line for a "Production" environment. Try using that line instead of what you're using now, restart Apache/PHP, and that should get rid of the errors. I'm trying to connect DomainMOD to my domain registrar account using the API so that I can import my domains, but everything in the Domain Queue just says "Pending" In order to import your domains using the domain registrar's API you must set up the cron job that comes with DomainMOD. In addition to having the cron job running, you must also have your API credential saved along with your registrar account Asset. (Domains you add without an API don't need any API credentials, but they still need the cron job.) I'm trying to import data using the Domain Queue, but everything is stuck on "Processing" In case there's an issue with the cron job you can also try triggering the queue manually. Go to Administration -> Task Scheduler , and then beside "Domain Queue Processing" click the "run now" link (this may take a bit of time to run). Then go back to the queue and see if anything has changed. If that doesn't work you can try clearing the queue items that are currently processing by going to Administration -> Cleanup , and then clicking on "Clear Queue Processing". Now try the last suggestion again to see if running the queue manually through the Task Scheduler helps. If that still doesn't do it go to Administration -> Cleanup , and then click on "Clear Queues". This deletes every list and domain in the Domain Queue, whatever their status (the SSL Queue isn't affected). Now try retrieving your data again using the Domain Queue. I've setup the Data Warehouse within DomainMOD, but none of my changes propagate to my web server The Data Warehouse is read-only. You can import data from your web server into your Data Warehouse, but this data is for informational purposes only, and you can't edit your server data within DomainMOD and have it update your web server. This is something that will be worked on in the future, but is currently not possible. After upgrading, I'm getting the error "Unable to verify the SSL certificate of a remote server" As of v4.24.02, DomainMOD checks the SSL certificate of every server it connects to, such as your registrars' APIs, your Data Warehouse servers, and the update check. This error means a server's certificate couldn't be verified, so DomainMOD didn't connect to it. The error names the service and includes the cURL error, which can help narrow down the cause. To fix it: Check that your server's date and time are correct. If the clock is wrong, valid certificates can look expired. Update your operating system's CA certificates (on most Linux systems this is the ca-certificates package). If curl.cainfo , openssl.cafile , or openssl.capath in your php.ini points to a file or folder that's missing or out of date, fix the path or remove the setting, then restart Apache/PHP. If your server connects to the internet through a proxy that inspects HTTPS traffic, add the proxy's CA certificate to your server's trusted certificates. If the error is for a Data Warehouse server with a self-signed certificate, the best fix is to give that server a valid certificate, or to add its certificate (or the CA that signed it) to your DomainMOD server's trusted CA certificates. As a last resort, if you connect to it over a network you trust, you can switch off Verify SSL Certificate? for that server only (see Data Warehouse Setup ). With it off, DomainMOD can't tell whether it's talking to your real server, so anyone able to intercept the connection could see your WHM API Token or Remote Access Key. If you see "Unable to connect to a remote server" instead, DomainMOD couldn't reach the server, so check your server's network connection and firewall. "A remote server didn't respond in time" means the server took too long to connect or answer, so check that the remote service is up and that your server can reach it, then try again. I'm getting the error, "Database Connection Error: 1045" Error 1045 is an access denied error, which seems to be caused when the user doesn't have appropriate permissions on the database, or there's another privilege issue with the database. Unfortunately this is pretty difficult to troubleshoot on our end, as there are many things that can cause this. We would recommend trying some of the suggestions for this error in Google and see if any of them help: https://www.google.com/search?q=Database+Connection+Error%3A+1045 . Form fields aren't displaying properly, such as checkboxes and text fields showing as empty boxes This is usually caused by JavaScript being disabled in your web browser. If enabling JavaScript doesn't fix the issue try disabling any ad blockers or other content blockers you may have installed. The currency conversions aren't working properly My fees are all showing up as zero This is usually caused by a currency converter that's experiencing downtime. You can fix this by changing the currency conversion source. Click Administration on the main menu, then click System Settings . Click on the Currency Converter dropdown menu and choose a new source. Click the Update System Settings button. After the Currency Converter source has been changed you can force a currency conversion update by going to Administration -> Task Scheduler , and then clicking the "run now" link beside "Update Conversion Rates". As of v4.27.0, you can also click Update Conversion Rates under Maintenance on the main menu, which updates only your own rates. I want to send email through a local mail relay that has no encryption and no sign-in As of v4.27.0, go to Administration -> System Settings , turn on Use SMTP Server? , and enter the relay's SMTP Server and SMTP Server Port , and the SMTP Email Address to send from. Choose None for SMTP Server Protocol , and leave SMTP Username and SMTP Password blank (tick Remove the saved value if a password is saved), then click Update System Settings . Only use None for a server like this. Any other SMTP server should use TLS or SSL. Times in my region are an hour off System Information says my time zone data is out of date Outdated PHP time zone data can make times appear an hour off in regions that recently changed their rules. As of v4.27.0, Administration -> System Information shows the PHP Time Zone Database version and warns you when it's older than DomainMOD expects. To fix it, update PHP or add the latest timezonedb PHP extension. If you can't do this yourself, your web hosting provider should be able to assist you. DomainMOD says it can't write to its temp folder, and restores are turned off As of v4.27.0, the web server needs to be able to write to DomainMOD's 'temp' folder and the files in it, including temp/restore.lock. DomainMOD keeps working without it, but restores stay turned off until it can. Give the user PHP runs as for your web server write access to the folder (see Installing ), and if your cron job runs as a different user, give that user write access too. My export ends with a row saying it's incomplete That row means the export stopped early because of an error, so the file is missing data. As of v4.27.0, exports are written out as they're read, which lets very large exports work. Try the export again, and if it keeps happening, turn on Debugging Mode (see Debugging ) and check the Debug Log and your PHP error log. Debugging If you're still having issues you can enable Debugging Mode, which will make DomainMOD start logging your actions and errors, which can help us troubleshoot your issue. Note No sensitive information gets stored in the debugging log. Passwords, API keys, and other sensitive information is replaced with asterisks, so we will never be able to view your private data. To enable Debugging Mode: Click Administration on the main menu, then click System Settings . Turn on the Debugging Mode switch. Click the Update System Settings button. Once debugging is enabled use DomainMOD as you normally would, repeating the steps you took when you first encountered the issue. Once you've done this continue with the below steps. If you haven't already, post about your issue in the Support Portal . If you're a developer and can point to the code, you can submit a GitHub issue instead. In DomainMOD, click on Administration and then Debug Log . Click the Export button to export the debugging log. In addition to the debugging log you should also retrieve your PHP error log, which will give us additional information about your issue. To find the location of your PHP error log: In DomainMOD, click on Administration and then System Information . Look for the heading named PHP Error Log Location . This will show you the location of the PHP error log on your web server. Once you have both your debugging log and PHP error log send an email to debugging@domainmod.org and attach the log files. Please also include the URL to your Support Portal post or GitHub issue so that we can determine the issue you're contacting us about. We will review your logs and get back to you as soon as we can! Also, if you haven't already, make sure you disable Debugging Mode. Helper Programs If all else fails, DomainMOD has some "helper" programs that support can supply you with in order to help investigate or fix your issue. Helper programs are nothing more than simple scripts that can perform actions on your DomainMOD installation, whether it's performing an update on your database or setting a temporary variable. Although helpers are generally custom and specific to the user's issue, we wanted to include a generic helper publicly so that users could get a feel for what helpers are and what they do. In DomainMOD v4.18, we implemented strict Content Security Policy headers in order to help secure the application and reduce the risk of certain web-based attacks. We also enabled forced HTTPS, which ensures that your DomainMOD installation will only work if you've secured your web hosting with an SSL certificate. Although we highly recommend keeping the CSP headers enabled, as well as using an SSL certificate to secure your DomainMOD installation, we realize that some users may not always be able to have these features enabled. If you're one of those users, and you need to disable CSP and HTTPS, you could use the below helper to do so. You would simply create the file /helpers/top.php and paste the below contents into it. That's all there is to it! The next time your visit your DomainMOD installation CSP and forced HTTPS will both be disabled. <?php // Contents of: /helpers/top.php $disable_csp = 1; $force_https = 0; Warning If you're using a helper to investigate or fix something, and the helper is only intended to be used temporarily, don't forget to delete the helper file as soon as you're done using it!

docs.text: Warning Before upgrading it's strongly recommended that you backup your DomainMOD installation directory and database. If something goes wrong during the upgrade there may be no way to recover your data, and having a backup of your installation directory and database will allow you to easily restore your previous version. The Backup & Restore instructions can be found here . As of v4.27.0, administrators can open Administration -> Upgrade to see the installed and latest versions, check for a new version with Check Now , and get the upgrade steps for the way DomainMOD was installed (Docker, Git, zip file, or Softaculous), with buttons to copy each command. If it detects the wrong installation method, choose yours under Not right? Choose yours and click Show Steps , or set $install_type in /_includes/config.inc.php . The steps for each method are also below. Option #1 -- Docker Install If you installed DomainMOD using Docker, please see our official DomainMOD container on Docker Hub for upgrade information: https://hub.docker.com/r/domainmod/domainmod Option #2 -- .zip File Install If you installed DomainMOD by downloading the .zip file, visit the following URL to download the most up-to-date version: https://domainmod.org/download/ Once the download completes, upload and unpack the new archive overtop of where you installed the previous version (or unpack it and then upload it, whichever you prefer). Option #3 -- Git Install If you installed DomainMOD using Git right from your web server, just run the following command from within your installation directory to upgrade: git pull Option #4 -- Softaculous Install If you installed DomainMOD using Softaculous you're just a few clicks away from upgrading to the newest version. Please see the upgrade instructions on the Softaculous Wiki: https://www.softaculous.com/docs/How_to_upgrade_installations Once the new files are in place, sign in as an administrator, and DomainMOD asks you to upgrade the database. Click Upgrade Database . While the upgrade runs, other pages say that DomainMOD is busy, so wait for it to finish. After Upgrading Unless you upgraded using Docker, restart PHP so the updated translation files are loaded (restart PHP-FPM if your server uses it, otherwise restart your web server). Otherwise some text may display incorrectly until it restarts. If you can't restart it yourself, your web hosting provider should be able to do it for you. As of v4.27.0, the web server needs to be able to write to the 'temp' folder and the files in it (see the Installation Steps ). If it can't, DomainMOD shows a warning and turns off restores until it can. Web Hosting Providers in v4.27.0 The v4.27.0 upgrade replaces each domain's Web Hosting Provider field with a hosting service . For each provider your domains used, it adds a hosting account with the username "Imported" for each owner, and under it a service named after the provider, then links those domains to it. Domains with the same provider and owner share one service. DomainMOD's placeholder providers, such as [no hosting], aren't converted. The old field had no other details, so each service starts as Active, with the service type Other, a 12-month billing term, auto-renew off, no fee, and a renewal date one year after the upgrade. After upgrading, open Hosting and update each service's details and renewal date, and the account's username, then add its fees. Set the service type and billing term first, since a fee applies to every service with the same provider, service type, and billing term.

docs.text: As of v4.27.0, the Watch List keeps track of domains you don't own yet, such as ones you'd like to buy or catch when they drop. DomainMOD checks each one in the background with public RDAP data, or WHOIS for TLDs without RDAP, and shows its expiry date, registrar, registry statuses, and stage, with an estimated drop date for generic TLDs. Requirement The checks are run by the Check Watch List task, so you must set up the cron job that comes with DomainMOD (Docker installs already run it), and keep the task enabled in the Task Scheduler . Adding Domains Click Watch List on the main menu. Click the Add Domains button. Paste in the domains you want to watch, one per line. Choose a Reason ( Want to buy , Backorder placed , Try to catch when it drops , Negotiating , or Just watching ), and add any Notes . Both are added to every domain on the list. Click the Add Domains button. The Watch List holds up to 1,000 domains, and archived domains don't count toward the limit. Domains you already have in DomainMOD can't be watched, unless they're Expired or Sold. Checks begin on the task's next scheduled run, which works through the list a few domains at a time. Stages Each domain's Stage comes from its latest check: Not checked yet , Checking , Checking again , or Unable to check : the domain hasn't been checked yet, a new result is being confirmed (see below), or the lookups have failed so far Registered or Newly registered : someone owns the domain Expiry date passed : the published expiry date has passed, but the registry hasn't reported a grace period Expired, in grace period : the registry reports the domain as expired, and the owner can usually still renew it In redemption : the owner can usually still restore the domain Restore pending : the owner has asked the registry to restore the domain Pending delete : the domain is about to be deleted, and usually can't be restored Not registered : the registry returned no record for the domain. It may be available, or it may be reserved, blocked, or offered at a premium price, so check with a registrar. A change into or out of Not registered is only recorded once a second lookup, about 15 minutes later, agrees with the first. Until then, the stage is Checking (for a new domain) or Checking again , and the domain's edit page says when the second lookup is due. The exception is a newly added or unarchived domain whose first RDAP answer says it isn't registered, which shows as Not registered straight away. How Often Domains Are Checked Registered domains are checked weekly while they're far from expiry, and daily in the last 60 days before they expire. Domains in the other stages are checked daily, and up to 50 domains that are close to dropping are checked every few hours. Failed checks are tried again less often each time, and a domain whose RDAP or WHOIS server is busy or limiting requests waits an hour. The Drop Estimate For generic TLDs (such as .com, .net, and .org), the Estimated Drop column shows the range of dates when the domain is likely to be deleted and become available, based on its statuses and ICANN's usual rules: up to 45 days of grace period, 30 days of redemption, and 5 days of pending delete. A Rough estimate is worked out during the grace period from the expiry date seen before it (so a domain first seen in grace has none), an Estimate from when redemption was first seen, and Likely from when pending delete was first seen. Other TLDs have their own rules, so their stage and statuses are still checked, but no drop date is estimated. Note Drop dates are only estimates, based on the domain's statuses and the TLD's usual rules. The owner can usually renew during the grace period and restore during redemption, so the domain may never drop. Once deletion is pending, it usually can't be restored. Popular names are often caught by paid backorder services the moment they drop, or never become available to register at all. A watched domain's page shows a similar note beside its estimate. The Watch List Page The list shows each domain's Stage , Expiry date, Registered date, Estimated Drop , Registrar , Reason , Added By , Last Checked , and Next Check . "(not updated)" beside a Last Checked time means the latest check didn't get an answer, so the details are from an earlier one. You can filter the list by Stage , Reason , TLD , Estimated Drop (Next 7 days, Next 30 days, or Any estimate), Added By , and whether it's Archived . To change several domains at once, tick them, choose Archive , Unarchive , Change the reason , or Delete from the With the selected domains menu, then click Apply . Export downloads the list as a CSV file, and Changes opens the watched domains' Change History . A Watched Domain's Page Click a domain to open its page, where you can: change its Reason and Notes see its current state, including its registry statuses and registration date click Check Now to look it up straight away (within 10 minutes of the last check, it shows that check's details instead) Archive it, which stops the checks and keeps the entry and its history, or Unarchive it, which starts watching it again from scratch Delete it (its earlier changes stay in the Change History) view its public RDAP record I Own This Now Once you've bought a watched domain, the I Own This Now section on its page opens a form to add it to your domains with its name filled in, using either Import with RDAP (recommended) , which adds it through the Domain Queue , or Add Manually . Once the domain is in your domains and isn't Expired or Sold, DomainMOD archives the watched domain automatically. If the domain is already in DomainMOD as Expired or Sold, set its Domain Status to Active and save instead, then use Refresh to update its details. Turning the Watch List Off The Watch List is on by default. If you don't use it, an administrator can turn off Use the Watch List in Administration -> System Settings , under Watch List , then click Update Watch List Setting . This hides it from every user and stops its checks. Your watched domains are kept, so turning it back on brings everything back.
docs.title: Watch List

docs.text: Click Watch List on the main menu. Click the Add Domains button. Paste in the domains you want to watch, one per line. Choose a Reason ( Want to buy , Backorder placed , Try to catch when it drops , Negotiating , or Just watching ), and add any Notes . Both are added to every domain on the list. Click the Add Domains button. The Watch List holds up to 1,000 domains, and archived domains don't count toward the limit. Domains you already have in DomainMOD can't be watched, unless they're Expired or Sold. Checks begin on the task's next scheduled run, which works through the list a few domains at a time.
docs.title: Adding Domains

docs.text: Each domain's Stage comes from its latest check: Not checked yet , Checking , Checking again , or Unable to check : the domain hasn't been checked yet, a new result is being confirmed (see below), or the lookups have failed so far Registered or Newly registered : someone owns the domain Expiry date passed : the published expiry date has passed, but the registry hasn't reported a grace period Expired, in grace period : the registry reports the domain as expired, and the owner can usually still renew it In redemption : the owner can usually still restore the domain Restore pending : the owner has asked the registry to restore the domain Pending delete : the domain is about to be deleted, and usually can't be restored Not registered : the registry returned no record for the domain. It may be available, or it may be reserved, blocked, or offered at a premium price, so check with a registrar. A change into or out of Not registered is only recorded once a second lookup, about 15 minutes later, agrees with the first. Until then, the stage is Checking (for a new domain) or Checking again , and the domain's edit page says when the second lookup is due. The exception is a newly added or unarchived domain whose first RDAP answer says it isn't registered, which shows as Not registered straight away.
docs.title: Stages

docs.text: Registered domains are checked weekly while they're far from expiry, and daily in the last 60 days before they expire. Domains in the other stages are checked daily, and up to 50 domains that are close to dropping are checked every few hours. Failed checks are tried again less often each time, and a domain whose RDAP or WHOIS server is busy or limiting requests waits an hour.
docs.title: How Often Domains Are Checked

docs.text: For generic TLDs (such as .com, .net, and .org), the Estimated Drop column shows the range of dates when the domain is likely to be deleted and become available, based on its statuses and ICANN's usual rules: up to 45 days of grace period, 30 days of redemption, and 5 days of pending delete. A Rough estimate is worked out during the grace period from the expiry date seen before it (so a domain first seen in grace has none), an Estimate from when redemption was first seen, and Likely from when pending delete was first seen. Other TLDs have their own rules, so their stage and statuses are still checked, but no drop date is estimated. Note Drop dates are only estimates, based on the domain's statuses and the TLD's usual rules. The owner can usually renew during the grace period and restore during redemption, so the domain may never drop. Once deletion is pending, it usually can't be restored. Popular names are often caught by paid backorder services the moment they drop, or never become available to register at all. A watched domain's page shows a similar note beside its estimate.
docs.title: The Drop Estimate

docs.text: The list shows each domain's Stage , Expiry date, Registered date, Estimated Drop , Registrar , Reason , Added By , Last Checked , and Next Check . "(not updated)" beside a Last Checked time means the latest check didn't get an answer, so the details are from an earlier one. You can filter the list by Stage , Reason , TLD , Estimated Drop (Next 7 days, Next 30 days, or Any estimate), Added By , and whether it's Archived . To change several domains at once, tick them, choose Archive , Unarchive , Change the reason , or Delete from the With the selected domains menu, then click Apply . Export downloads the list as a CSV file, and Changes opens the watched domains' Change History .
docs.title: The Watch List Page

docs.text: Click a domain to open its page, where you can: change its Reason and Notes see its current state, including its registry statuses and registration date click Check Now to look it up straight away (within 10 minutes of the last check, it shows that check's details instead) Archive it, which stops the checks and keeps the entry and its history, or Unarchive it, which starts watching it again from scratch Delete it (its earlier changes stay in the Change History) view its public RDAP record
docs.title: A Watched Domain's Page

docs.text: Once you've bought a watched domain, the I Own This Now section on its page opens a form to add it to your domains with its name filled in, using either Import with RDAP (recommended) , which adds it through the Domain Queue , or Add Manually . Once the domain is in your domains and isn't Expired or Sold, DomainMOD archives the watched domain automatically. If the domain is already in DomainMOD as Expired or Sold, set its Domain Status to Active and save instead, then use Refresh to update its details.
docs.title: I Own This Now

docs.text: The Watch List is on by default. If you don't use it, an administrator can turn off Use the Watch List in Administration -> System Settings , under Watch List , then click Update Watch List Setting . This hides it from every user and stops its checks. Your watched domains are kept, so turning it back on brings everything back.
